text:
Newhouse votes for appropriations bill to support national security and allies
Rep. Dan Newhouse announced on July 15 that he voted in favor of the National Security, Department of State, and Related Programs Appropriations Act of 2027. The legislation passed the House with a vote of 217-209.
“At a time when our Nation’s national security is under constant threat from adversaries, we are delivering on legislation to provide resources to critical agencies that keep us safe," said Rep. Dan Newhouse.
Newhouse also said, "Peace through strength will ensure the United States remains the shining city on the hill as a diplomatic and economic powerhouse. I applaud Chairman Diaz-Balart’s efforts to eliminate wasteful spending while prioritizing the programs that keep Americans safe.”
The appropriations bill provides a total discretionary allocation of $47.32 billion, which is $2.69 billion or six percent below the Fiscal Year 2026 enacted level. The measure maintains funding for allies such as Israel, Jordan, Egypt, and Taiwan while aiming to counter adversaries including China, Iran, Cuba, and drug cartels designated as Foreign Terrorist Organizations. The bill aligns with executive orders intended to refocus foreign policy priorities.
Dan Newhouse has served in Congress representing Washington's 4th District since 2015 after previously serving in the Washington House of Representatives from 2003 to 2009; he succeeded Doc Hastings in Congress and currently resides in Sunnyside where he was born in 1955; he graduated from Washington State University in 1977 with a Bachelor of Science degree, according to the office of Dan Newhouse.
